key_insight: A target-ω model damps interfacial turbulence in stratified gas–liquid RANS simulations without calibrating model constants against target data.
engineering_relevance: The formulation supports prediction of gas-side flow and turbulence in stratified two-phase systems with reduced sensitivity to near-interface mesh resolution.
method: Integrates interfacial damping into a low-Reynolds-number Wilcox-type k–ω model within one-field RANS/VOF.
Constructs a gas-side target ω from an effective interfacial wall coordinate derived from the local resolved flow.
Uses power-law blending to transition smoothly between viscous and logarithmic limits.
evidence_signal: Assessment against three gas-layer DNS cases at Reτ ≈ 180 and the Fabre co-current and Stäbler counter-current experiments showed generally good gas-side predictions, with close agreement for Stäbler’s mean liquid depth.
watch_item: Some grid dependence remains on the coarsest mesh, and validation is limited to the resolved-interface conditions studied.
paper_title: Development and assessment of a target-$ω$ interfacial turbulence-damping model for stratified gas--liquid flow
